newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-FORMER CHAMPIONS GREMIO SUFFER SHOCK DEFEAT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-FORMER CHAMPIONS GREMIO SUFFER SHOCK DEFEAT.

text.p: Former Libertadores Cup champions Gremio suffered a shock defeat against litte-known Paraguayans Guarani in the second round of the South American Libertadores Cup on Wednesday.

Defending champions River Plate, playing their opening match in the competition, drew 3-3 away to fellow Argentines Racing Club while 1994 winners Velez Sarsfield, also from Argentina, drew 0-0 away to Sporting Cristal of Peru.
Brazil's Gremio, who seldom seem to get through a match in the competition with all 11 players still on the field, had a player and their coach sent off in the first leg match in Asuncion.

Guarani, who live in the shadows of their country's traditional powers Cerro Porteno and Olimpia and are in the competition for the first time in 12 years, won with goals by Hugo Ovelar in the fourth and 82nd minutes.
In between Andre Silva equalised for Gremio, winners in 1983 and 1995.

Ovelar's winner came shortly after after Gremio's Paraguayan international defender Catalino Rivarola was sent off for a second bookable offence. Coach Evaristo Macedo was also dismissed near the end after a row with the referee.
The Defenders of the Chaco stadium, usually packed when Cerro Porteno or Olimpia play in the tournament, was nearly deserted with Guarani's tiny support only able to muster around 2,500 fans.
River Plate, who as champions had a bye to the second round, twice trailed and then led 3-2 before settling for a draw against the team coached by Alfio Basile, Argentina's 1994 World Cup coach.
Five of the goals came in a dramatic first half before Claudio Ubeda salvaged a draw for Racing 12 minutes from time.

Velez, who meet the winners of the Racing-River clash in the quarter-finals, had Paraguayan goalkeeper Jose Luis Chilavert booked for time-wasting as they slugged out a 0-0 draw in Lima. Chilavert also fired one of his trademark free kicks into the Cristal wall during a rare Velez attack in the first half.
In the other ties played Wednesday, Bolivar of Bolivia drew 1-1 away to Minerven of Venezuela while Millonarios of Colombia beat Penarol 2-0 at home.

Millonarios dominated their match in Bogota against the five-times winners from Uruguay but had to wait until the second half for their goals which came through Ricardo Perez, from a penalty, and Bonner Mosquera.
Boliviar should have little trouble completing an aggregate win at home in La Paz, 3,600 metres above sea level.
